47D6SX.position: You bought this building in the spring of 2012, while the market was still finding its footing, at a basis of ±$65 per square foot — and you did it the smart way: your own operation under your own roof in Riverside's Hunter Park. Fourteen years later, the same square footage trades at well over three times that number, and your building holds a card most of the competition can't match: 2003 construction — the newest product in this size band anywhere in the submarket — on a ±2.13-acre parcel with direct access to the SR-60 and I-215. The owner-users and investors hunting for modern, sub-40,000 SF warehouse space in Riverside have almost nowhere to look, and that scarcity is your leverage. Because you both own and occupy, every option is on the table: sell into that demand at the top of the range, capture the equity through a sale-leaseback while your operation stays exactly where it is, or trade up to a larger facility timed so you never miss a day of business. Whichever direction you choose, the equity is already there — the only question is when and how you capture it.
47D6SX.comps_source: C&W / CoStar verified sales, Inland Empire 10k–100k SF, trailing 18 months (July 2026 set)
